repaired.name: Scenario
repaired.script:
triggered := false
if (triggered == true) {
wait until(not (all(#ContactSensor).contactSensor_contact == false))
triggered = false
}
wait until(all(#ContactSensor).contactSensor_contact == false)
all(#Switch).switch_on()
triggered = true

diagnosis.summary: The IR requires a rising-edge wait for `ContactSensor.Contact == false` before calling `Switch.On`. The candidate uses a periodic `if` at the start of the cycle body, which only evaluates at t=0, t=1000, etc. At t=100, the condition became true, but the candidate missed it because the `if` guard was false at t=0 and the next evaluation was too late. This matches Example A (repeating rising edge implemented as periodic polling).
diagnosis.change_summary: Replaced the periodic `if` guard with a blocking two-wait rearm pattern: wait for the condition to become false (rising edge), then execute the body, then wait for it to become true again to rearm. This ensures the action fires exactly when the edge occurs, regardless of the wrapper period.
